content.intro: This lesson focuses on converting yaml to json and connects the PDF syllabus topics to a small, inspectable example. Work from the intended data model, write down the expected result, then verify syntax and semantics with the target tool.
content.why_it_matters: Converting YAML to JSON matters because structured-data files sit between people, tools, services, and deployment systems. A clear contract and repeatable checks make the result easier to maintain and safer to consume.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: JSON and YAML can often represent equivalent mappings, sequences, and scalar values, but conversion can change types, omit comments, expose duplicate keys, or alter formatting. Compare parsed values and document what the target tools preserve.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly addresses: Parsing YAML values. Handling mapping keys. Resolving scalar types. Handling anchors and aliases. Dealing with multiple documents.; Handling tags and non-JSON values. Detecting lossy conversions.. Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Converting YAML to JSON
content_blocks.code:
YAML input:
app:
  name: Field Notes
  enabled: true
ports: [8080, 8081]

JSON equivalent:
{
  "app": {"name": "Field Notes", "enabled": true},
  "ports": [8080, 8081]
}
content_blocks.expected_output: The JSON output preserves this sample data but cannot preserve YAML comments or arbitrary YAML-specific tags as ordinary JSON values.

content_blocks.text: Do not judge a conversion only by how the text looks. Parse both documents, compare values and types, and record features that cannot be represented on both sides. Confirm implementation-specific behavior against the target parser, tool version, and standards documentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating readable text as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Syntax and visual formatting cannot establish data types, schema conformance, or application-specific meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse, validate against the intended contract, and test a valid plus an invalid fixture.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every parser interprets the feature identically.
common_mistakes.why: Format versions, schema choices, library defaults, and product-specific restrictions affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the exact parser/version and test the target environment.

common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, wrong types, duplicate keys, or ambiguous scalars may still break consumers.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep valid, invalid, and boundary fixtures in version control.
